lesson_yaml:
schema: cairn/lesson/v0.1
id: go-tar-extraction-filepath-join-path-traversal
title: Tar entry name or link target joined to destination with filepath.Join instead of securejoin
summary: 'Names and link targets read from a tar header (`hdr.Name`, `hdr.Linkname`) are combined with
  the extraction root using `filepath.Join`. That join is purely lexical. It does not resolve symlinks
  planted by earlier entries and it does not reject `..` components. A crafted layer or archive can therefore
  write, hard-link or `os.RemoveAll` (via whiteout entries) outside the extraction root.

  '
cwe:
- CWE-22
- CWE-59
severity: high
confidence: medium

source:
  kind: fix-commit
  ref: a370e4b1f66e6e842b685c8f70ed507964c4b221
  vulnerable_ref: a370e4b1f66e6e842b685c8f70ed507964c4b221^

  repository: https://github.com/chainguard-forks/kaniko
rule:
  message: 'Path built from a tar entry using filepath.Join is only lexically joined. Symlinks and `..`
    in the archive can escape the extraction root. Resolve with securejoin.SecureJoin(root, name) and
    reject names that reference the parent directory.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern-either:
    - pattern: '$P := filepath.Join($D, $N)

        '
    - pattern: '$P := filepath.Clean(filepath.Join($D, $H.Linkname))

        '
  - pattern-either:
    - pattern-inside: "func $F(..., $HDR *tar.Header, ...) error {\n  ...\n}\n"
    - pattern-inside: "func $F(...) ($A, error) {\n  ...\n  tar.NewReader(...)\n  ...\n}\n"
    - pattern-inside: "func $F(...) error {\n  ...\n  tar.NewReader(...)\n  ...\n}\n"
  - pattern-not-inside: "func $F(...) error {\n  ...\n  securejoin.SecureJoin(...)\n  ...\n}\n"
  - pattern-not-inside: "func $F(...) ($A, error) {\n  ...\n  securejoin.SecureJoin(...)\n  ...\n}\n"
fix:
  guidance: 'Do not build extraction paths with filepath.Join on tar entry names or link targets. Use
    github.com/cyphar/filepath-securejoin SecureJoin(root, name), which resolves symlinks and keeps the
    result inside root. Also reject cleaned names equal to ".." or starting with "../". For symlink entries,
    resolve the target relative to the entry''s parent directory and refuse targets that land outside
    the destination. Hard-link targets need the same treatment.

    '
  example: "cleaned := filepath.Clean(hdr.Name)\nif cleaned == \"..\" || strings.HasPrefix(cleaned, \"\
    ../\") {\n    return fmt.Errorf(\"tar entry %q references parent directory\", hdr.Name)\n}\npath,\
    \ err := securejoin.SecureJoin(dest, cleaned)\nif err != nil {\n    return fmt.Errorf(\"resolving\
    \ path for %q: %w\", hdr.Name, err)\n}\nf, err := os.Create(path)\n"
